title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to measure whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 programmatically generated synthetic intents, model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled candidate reused across baseline and guarded conditions), guarded pipeline permitted at most one repair per intent. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1; shared_initial_generation = 150. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We document why this ceiling effect invalidated the preregistered power assumptions and recommend concrete preregistration and pilot-calibration prescriptions for future NetOps trials. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle (preregistration SHA-256 and master-prompt reference included in the Disclosure Statement).

sections.introduction: Natural-language intent interfaces promise to reduce operator burden by expressing desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work shows that single-pass LLM outputs frequently contain syntactic errors, omissions, or ordering violations that can produce unsafe or unavailable device states if applied directly. A widely proposed mitigation is a generate→verify→repair architecture: an LLM produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants, and an automated repair or human gate corrects violations before execution. Motivated by this operational picture, we preregistered a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increases deterministic-verifier semantic correctness of NL→configuration translations versus an unconstrained baseline. The preregistered trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) and its analysis plan were frozen before any model outputs were observed.
sections.related_work: Related literature spans three strands. First, intent-to-configuration evaluations report modest semantic-correctness rates for unconstrained LLM prompting and show sensitivity to prompt design, model competence, and oracle choice. Second, generate→verify→repair systems (including verifier-in-the-loop IaC efforts) report practical correctness improvements, but effect sizes depend strongly on baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, sampling semantics, and repair budgets. Third, deterministic network-verification tools (NetKAT/KATch family and related symbolic engines) can serve as concrete oracles for reachability and policy checks; they return compact diagnostics useful for automated repair but vary in protocol and scale support. Security analyses additionally warn that unguarded multi-tool agents can convert false textual claims into harmful actions and motivate auditable, conservative gating. Our trial explicitly operationalizes three design choices emphasized by prior work: (1) repair budget (≤1 repair), (2) sampling/execution semantics (shared_initial_candidate), and (3) deterministic verifier as the binary correctness oracle. These choices shape the estimand and interpretability of any marginal repair benefit.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and froze a paired confirmatory design before observing outcomes. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated with an exact two-sided McNemar test on deterministic-verifier pass/fail outcomes; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval used 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration specified N=150 confirmatory intents, deterministic inclusion/exclusion rules (rule-based ambiguity detector, parser/verifier-coverage checks), a one-retry policy for provider timeouts, and a power target to detect an absolute +15 percentage-point improvement under conservative discordant-pair assumptions. All preregistration elements (estimands, inclusion rules, multiplicity plan, analysis scripts) were archived prior to model calls.

Model, validator, and execution adapter. Declared model in execution metadata: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses); recorded model_configuration.json notes declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). Because no numeric temperature or fixed random seed was enforced, independent API sessions may produce nondeterministic outputs; the preregistration anticipated this sampling uncertainty and specified execution semantics. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail plus normalized_configuration and per-episode diagnostics. The execution adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced the preregistered call-budget and execution semantics and recorded provider accounting.

Execution semantics mapping and preregistration labels. The preregistration conceptually labeled three conditions (A: baseline free-text prompt, B: constrained-template prompt, C: constrained + verifier-feedback). Important clarification required by the confirmatory run and reviewer guidance: the archived execution enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics. Concretely, for each intent the adapter produced exactly one initial model generation and that identical sampled candidate was reused for paired evaluation under baseline (A) and guarded (C) conditions; the guarded pipeline was permitted at most one additional repair call only if the verifier failed that shared initial candidate. Therefore, although the preregistration described a conceptual three-arm design and hypotheses H1/H2 over A/B/C, the archived run and the primary estimand evaluate the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to the same initial sampled candidate—i.e., the executed and archived primary contrast is guarded (C) versus baseline (A) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The constrained-only condition (B) was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run (no independent B-vs-A confirmatory contrast was produced); this mapping is deliberate and enforced by the adapter. All analysis reported below follows the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 and no post-preregistration nor post-lock modifications to the confirmatory analysis were performed.

Task generation, prechecks, and inclusion. Confirmatory tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across four intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like changes, VLAN/MTU sequences, uplink switchover patterns). Topologies were constrained to 4–32 nodes to ensure deterministic verifier coverage. Parser-to-verifier mapping unit-tests specified in the preregistration were executed and passed before batch execution. Deterministic exclusion rules (ambiguous intents routed to exploratory corpus; parse failures or unsupported verifier features excluded with recorded reason codes) were applied prior to model calls; in the archived run no confirmatory exclusions occurred.

Operational budgets and analysis treatment. The adapter enforced a strict call budget: one initial generation per intent shared across conditions and at most one permitted repair call for guarded episodes if the verifier failed the shared candidate. Primary analysis used only complete paired episodes (complete_pair_primary). Sensitivity analyses treating missing guarded outputs as failures were preregistered but not invoked because there were no failed or unscorable episodes in the archived run. All provider traces, shared_initial_response files, and validator traces were archived to enable deterministic reconciliation.
sections.results:
Execution and provider audit. The run completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count = 300 (150 intents × 2 conditions) and completed_episode_count = 300. Provider-call accounting (artifact-grounded): model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts recorded by the adapter: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. No contamination flags or pre-execution unit-test failures occurred and no confirmatory exclusions were recorded.

Primary numerical outcomes. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv are: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These values are reported verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and iteration counts. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. That single repair converted one initially failing shared candidate to a verifier-valid configuration. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces (validation_before and validation_after) with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_codes are archived for every episode; representative traces for tasks 000001–000006 are included in the execution bundle and confirm validator behavior.

Representative example. Task-000001 (generator_seed = 1) intent: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up. Do not modify any other interface." The shared-initial candidate and both condition responses produced the four-command sequence required by the preregistered reference answer. Validator diagnostics: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, valid = true. The shared_initial_response and normalized_configuration strings for this and other representative tasks are archived in execution/responses and scoring traces.

Power and ceiling observation. The preregistered power calculation targeted detection of an absolute +15 pp improvement with ≈80% power under conservative discordant-pair assumptions. The observed baseline_success_rate ≈99.33% left essentially no headroom for a large absolute improvement, producing a ceiling effect that invalidated the preregistered detectable-effect assumption and reduced the trial's discriminative information (very low discordant-pair counts). This inferential consequence is reflected in the contingency where n_10 + n_01 = 1, leaving the McNemar test with effectively no evidence of discordance. As stated above, no post-preregistration changes to the confirmatory analysis were made; reported analyses follow the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and methodological implications. The principal scientific lesson from this preregistered trial is methodological: confirmatory NetOps trials that expect substantial absolute improvements from verifier-guided repair must first assess baseline competence. When intents are tightly specified by the generator and verifier coverage matches the required invariants, single sampled candidates from capable LLMs may already satisfy the verifier, producing near-ceiling baselines and invalidating preregistered power assumptions. We therefore recommend a mandatory baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., 20–40 tasks) to estimate baseline_success_rate and discordant-pair proportions before final N selection or difficulty tuning. The archived deterministic task generator seeds and representative tasks permit reproducible pilots against the same generator.

Sampling semantics, estimand interpretation, and operational trade-offs. The shared_initial_candidate semantics used here isolate the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to the same initial sampled candidate; alternative semantics answer different operational questions. Independent per-condition sampling estimates expected verifier pass rates averaging over fresh model draws for each pipeline; multi-draw or larger repair budgets estimate cost–benefit trade-offs between additional model calls and improved correctness. Practitioners must align sampling semantics, repair budgets, and cost/latency constraints with the estimand they intend to measure and preregister those choices accordingly.

Operational affordances beyond binary pass/fail. Even when the guarded pipeline yields a numerically small verifier-pass difference, deterministic validators produce normalized_configuration strings, explicit violation codes, and other diagnostics that improve operational observability and triage. These secondary artifacts (archived per-episode validator traces) can accelerate human review or feed automated repair policies and are valuable even when marginal verifier-pass improvements are small on constrained corpora.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: adapter-enforced call budgets and provider audits mitigated cross-condition leakage; mapping unit-tests reduced parse/translation failures. Construct validity: deterministic verifier pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; any uncovered verifier-coverage gap would bias measurement. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks on small topologies (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to larger, heterogeneous WANs or different models. Security and adversarial robustness: this confirmatory trial did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection; separate targeted studies are required. Conclusion validity: the mismatch between preregistered detectable-effect assumptions and observed baseline underlines the need for pilot calibration to preserve inferential validity.

Practical prescriptions. Based on artifact-grounded outcomes we recommend: (1) an explicit baseline-calibration pilot before confirmatory sampling; (2) preregistration that explicitly states sampling/execution semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent draws) and repair budgets; (3) multi-arm designs varying repair budgets and sampling semantics to estimate cost–benefit frontiers; (4) inclusion of provider-call accounting in power and cost planning; and (5) staged scaling of verifier coverage with deterministic mapping unit-tests. The archived execution manifest and representative tasks provide concrete seeds and runnable code to implement these prescriptions reproducibly.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On the preregistered synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The main scientific contribution is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials must include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating alternative sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies is necessary future work. All runtime traces, verifier logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
